Question: How does India’s Railways’ corporate train model work?
Answer: Recently, IRCTC introduced Kashi Mahakal Express which is the country's third corporate train after two Tejas Exp trains between Delhi-Lucknow and Mumbai-Ahmedabad. All corporate trains are running with a new model which is actively pushed by Indian Railways to ' out source' the running of regular passenger trains. What is a Corporate Model? The Physical infrastructure of the train such as locomotives, coaches, locopilots among others will remain in Indisn Railway's hand. However, the services provided including ticketing and refunds, parcels, catering and housekeeping will be outsourced to the Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation and other such companies who will operate corporate trains in the future. Outsourcing the trains will help Indian Railways to earn a predecided fixed amount after every run based on three components and the owner of the network will be Indian Railways. Three components are: 1. Haulage : Operational amount paid to move a rake. For example: Track, Signalling, Locopilots and other physical involvement required to run a rake. IRCTC is paying INR 800/ Km to Railways for Lucknow Tejas. 2. Liese : Amount paid to Indian Railway Finance Corporation for the liece of coaches and locomotive. 3. Custody: Per day charges for the custody of rake which also includes maintainance cost which is around 2 lakh of one day in case of Lucknow Tejas. IRCTC is paying a sum total of 14 Lakh ( approx) per day ( up & down run) to the Indian Railways ( For Lucknow Tejas Express). • This is a fixed amount which IRCTC has to pay for every run, No matter train is running empty or full. IRCTC also shares a fixed profit precentage to the Railways. What are the powers that corporate entity will have? 1. As they are paying a heavy liece and custody amount to the railways so they have the suthority to select the rake and for sure every time a new rake will be asked for operation of any new train 2. IRCTC can change the service parameters itself without any approval from the ministry of railways. 3. Power of deciding the number of halts on decided route of any train. ☆The bright side for Indian Railways is that it doesn't have to suffer the losses in associated with running the trains. What is different between Private trains and corporate trains? Private trains are goods trains in which companies do not pay any liese and custody amount to the Railways. Highest bidding company gets the contract and they bring their own rolling stock. In case of Corporate trains, companies take the coaches on lease from the Indian Railways. Question: Why do some train stations have only one passenger platform but has 2 railways? How does a train from the opposite side go to the other?
Answer: India, being a massive country, has one of the largest railway networks in the world, which operates close to 28000 trains (passenger and freight) daily. There are almost 7400 railway stations in the Indian railway network to manage the smooth operations of the Indian Railways. The purpose of developing a railway station is not only to provide a platform for passengers but also to manage the massive traffic on Indian tracks. If we observe the network, we can find a railway station after every 4–8 km, and there is a reason behind that. Not all stations are purposely opened for passengers; some do not have a lot of foot fall, but they are very important for the railways. But why? So, the purpose of building a railway station after every 4–8 km and developing at least 2 railway tracks is to manage train operations properly. A second track is helpful in: i) Crossing: If two trains are supposed to cross each other, this scenario is common and useful on sections with single tracks. In that case, trains can only cross each other at these railway stations. Developing a raikway station after every 4–8 km helps in reducing the wait time for each train. ii) Overtake: If one train has to overtake the other train, in such senarios, railway stations play an important role in both single-line and double-line sections. iii) For idle rakes: Sometimes we find an empty rake at Railway Statiins. Generally, they are idled at slightly bigger stations so that the station is able to keep at least 2 tracks free for operations, but if necessary, small stations with 2 tracks use the loop line (second track) for idle rakes. iv) In case of technical failures or accidents: The second track always helps in these scenarios to park such trains and keep the main line clear for other trains. These were a few major benefits of having at least one extra track at railway stations. Mostly there is no second platform at railway stations is because of low footfall at that particular station, and in such cases, platform no. 1 is used for passenger trains so that people can easily board or deboard. Building a plstform and keeping operational requires a decent amount of money which railway avoids to spend if the foot fall at that railway station is low but a second track is important for the reasons I mentioned above. -Prashant Tiwari ✍️. Thank you for your valuable time.

Question: What is the auto upgradation feature shown while booking a train ticket?
Answer: If you often book your train tickets online then you have surely seen an option named Auto Upgradation on the booking page. I'll try to go into detail about this feature and also discuss its purpose. What is auto upgradation? Auto upgradation is a complementary feature offered by railways to all its passengers, which upgrades their ticket to the higher class if seats are available after the first chart is prepared. How does it work? Suppose you have booked a confirmed train ticket in 3AC and opted for auto upgradation. Now at the time of charting the system checked and found that there is a waiting list in 3 AC but there are 3 seats available in 2AC. In that case, the system will upgrade your ticket to 2AC and vacate a berth for RAC passengers of 3AC and allot RAC to the waiting list passengers. Isn't that cool, right? How is it beneficial for Railways? We all know that online waiting list tickets get canceled after first charting i.e., 4 hours prior to the train's departure time and IRCTC initiates the refund in 1-3 working days. With this feature, the system upgrades a few tickets to higher class and make some seats available in the class where demand is high and allot those seats to RAC passengers whereas Waiting list passengers get RAC and now they can travel. This way Railways reduces the cancellations and of course some amount which they had to refund in case of cancellations. You can opt for an auto upgradation feature for free while booking your train tickets through Trainman. It also provides an option of Trip Assurance, which guarantees your travel even if your ticket is in the waiting list. Follow the link to know more : P.S. Question: Does a bogie in a train mean the same as a coach or is it different?
Answer: Both are different. In the context of Indian Railways, "bogie" and "coach" are often used interchangeably, but there is a slight difference between the two. A "bogie" refers to the wheeled undercarriage that supports a train's cars or coaches. Each bogie typically has two or more axles with wheels attached to a frame that connects to the car or coach. A "coach" is the passenger-carrying car that is attached to the bogie. A coach can have several bogies attached to it, depending on its length and weight. Each coach typically has seats or berths for passengers, as well as amenities such as toilets, air conditioning, fans and lights. So in summary, a bogie is the wheeled undercarriage that supports a coach, while a coach is the passenger-carrying car that is attached to the bogie. -Prashant Tiwari ✍️. Question: Why do they give general class tickets only from the station of booking and not from any station to any station unlike reservation tickets in Indian Railways?
Answer: Logics behind everything in the Railways are very interesting. Last year, I planned to travel in an inaugral special train which was suppose to run between Sitapur Jn to Lucknow Jn. I was excited for the journey but I was aware that it will be very crowded at ticket counter as it is inaugral run so i planned to go on another station i.e., Sitapur city and asked for a general ticket from Sitapur Jn to Luvknow Jn. Person at the counter asked me to take ticket from Sitapur city to Lucknow Jn and ended up his line by ssying “ general ticket jis ststion pe ho vhi ka lena pdega” . I didn’t ask him more sbout this as there were many other people in the queue but later i tried to find the answer of my question Why railways do not allow to book general tickets of any station to any station from any station like reserved tickets? After searching on internet and asking few railway persons I came to few conclusive points: 1 . Most appropriate reason I found is allowing this facility we result into a heavy loss to the Railways. General tickets are mostly checked at the exit gates of the stations nkw taking an example lets say you are travelling from New Delhi to Lucknow and the cost of ticket is Rs.100 but misusing tjat facility you can buy a ticket from Alamnagar( nearest station to lucknow ) at New Delhi and a platform ticket of INR 10 which means you saved Rs 80 in your journey and you can easily complete your journey . To counter this type of loop hole Railways do not allow you to book your general ticket. In case of reserved tickets, TTE checks ticket in the train so you will be caught easily if your boarding station, train and date of journey is different. 2. This will increase the work of Ticket clerks or contractors. Every station prints a summary ticket at the end of the day which tells the amount earned and the no. of tickets sold from the particular station. On the basis of the station’s earning Railways decides the category of the station. In case of changing the source station there will be inappropriate data of earning from the particular station. There are few more points which I foind either irrelevent or somehow connected to the above mentioned points like serial ticket no. are also kept in the record that from ticket no. Xxxx to ticket no. Xxxx sold on a particular day from a particular station which directly effwcts on the facilities given to the station. More tickets more facilities. Hope you understand the basic reasons behind this. Question: How do I book a train coach for a wedding trip?
Answer: It is no secret that it takes considerable time, planning and effort to get a confirmed seat on a train via Indian Railways. But there are times when you are travelling with a big group of friends or family and wish to be seated near each other, or even in the same coach — something which can get a little tricky. But do not worry as it is something that can be done. IRCTC’s FTR service makes this process a lot easier and anyone can book either one or two coaches or a train as per the requirement. Before going through the process, there are few important things which everyone should know: 1 . The time span to book your coach for the wedding starts 6 months in advance and at least 30 days in advance before the journey date. 2. One can book maximum 7 coaches. 3. PAN card details is mandatory before booking. 4. One needs to crrate a new FTR account before booking a coach or a train. IRCTC’s account will not work here. 5. Booking amount covers a round trip and ptices are set accordingly. 6. Minimum booking amount for a coach is INR 50,000 and for a train is INR 9,00,000. 7. Booking amount is same for all type of coaches. 8. To add more coaches in a train , additional amount i.e., INR 10,000 will be charged per coach. Process Step by step: Step 1: Go to IRCTC Next Generation eTicketing System , scroll down and select chartered train. Step 2: You will be directed to a new page of IRCTC’s FTR services. You can alao directly reach to this page by http://www.ftrirctc.co.in . Step3: Create your account and enter all the required personal details (similar to irctc account) . Note: Here PAN card is mandatory. Step 4: Login to your account after email id and mobile number verification. A new window will pop up to your screen with two options A. Coach B. Train. Step 5: Select any one of the two as per the requirement. Note: on selecting coach, max 2 coaches can be booked in one train costing INR 50,000 each. Step 6: If you have opted to booked a train then anew window will be open and you meed to select type of coach, no. of coaches( two SLRs are mandatory), source and destination station, date of journey and time of journey . If you are opting a round trip then you need to fill all the details again for return journey. Reason for the journey is also asked on this page. Note: Amount will be charged for roundtrip even if you book a one way journey. Step 7: Now you can review you details and make payment. You can also book a train or coach by reaching to the chief reservation officer at the nearby station, discuss with him or her about the total number of passengers that needs to travel along with showing him or her with a wedding card as a proof for verification. Question: What are the MEMU EMU DMU trains? How does it work?
Answer: We all know that most of the trains are pulled by locomotive (engine), but in multiple unit sets like EMU/MEMU, multiple coaches are powered. It means that in ordinary train, only locomotive (engine) has a traction motor attached to it for running whole train. But in multiple unit trains, coaches are self propelled or you can say that coaches do not need any locomotive. All powered coaches are connected thorough MU (multiple unit) cable and all the motors of powered coaches are controlled by controller or motor man from any of the two ends. Due to this reason, multiple unit trains have a higher acceleration and retardation as compared to that of a normal locomotive hauled train. Difference between EMU, MEMU and DMU. DEMU( Diesel Electric Multiple Unit) , it works on the same principle as the diesel locomotives. Diesel genetator of 750 HP produces electricity which is fed to the traction motors of the power car and also in the trailer car having traction motor. Usually traction motors are provided at both ends of the rake. A new aerodynamic design of DEMU introduced in 2004 on the SCR. It consists of 8 car rakes (Two motor car and six Trailer cars ). ELECTRICAL MULTIPLE UNIT EMU are preffered for suburban section as it have high accerleration and phenomenal stopping distances allowing them to achieve higher speed at a short time and stopping efficiently hence it ultimately offers high throughput. Mainly two different emu's are in use , these are: • 1.5 KV DC traction • 25 KV AC traction MEMU's known as Main Line EMU. It was first introduced in 1993 by ICF so that it can be operated in more areas. Unlike the EMU's they have vestibule connection (gangway connection) and lavatories. MEMU motor car seats 76 and trailer coach 108 with a top speed of 105 kmph. They are equipped with electro-pneumatic brakes. Images : google Thank you for reading the answer.
